### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2302b92b1b4abc09bbf95995909d8656c8edf4cf`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2302b92b1b4abc09bbf95995909d8656c8edf4cf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `51ad112a64e9110810719abb5151436d641c9f80` — the merge of head `9727b5111f709fcd92d512e40cc3cbf145662564` into base `2302b92b1b4abc09bbf95995909d8656c8edf4cf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 51ad112a64e9110810719abb5151436d641c9f80 && git checkout 51ad112a64e9110810719abb5151436d641c9f80
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2302b92b1b4abc09bbf95995909d8656c8edf4cf 9727b5111f709fcd92d512e40cc3cbf145662564 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2302b92b1b4abc09bbf95995909d8656c8edf4cf && git merge --no-ff 9727b5111f709fcd92d512e40cc3cbf145662564

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2302b92b1b4abc09bbf95995909d8656c8edf4cf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2302b92b1b4abc09bbf95995909d8656c8edf4cf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, read against the cited code on `main`:

1. **`@objectstack/formula` template dialect, render accept set narrowed — right.** `templateEngine.evaluate` now refuses the whole sentence (`kind: 'runtime'`) when any `currency` hole has no argument and `ctx.currency` is not three capitals, before anything renders; `compile` and `validateExpression` are unchanged, so every authoring door (`objectstack validate`, `registerFlow`, the publish gate) accepts the hole as before. `firstTenantCurrencyHole` reads the same `HOLE_RE` / `parseHole` pair compile reads, so the pre-check and the formatter agree on what a no-argument hole is. The formatter's own `'USD'` fallback (`template-engine.ts:84` on `main`) is gone; nothing formats in US dollars.
2. **`formatValue('currency', v, undefined, opts)` throws without `opts.currency` — right**, and it throws whatever the value, as the `@path` value refusal of #26937 does: the judgment is of the hole, not the data.
3. **`EvalContext.currency` — right.** `buildScope` (`stdlib.ts:763`) binds only `record` / `previous` / `input` / the `os` namespace / `extra`, so the channel is never a root; the test that a root named `currency` stays a value holds against that code.
4. **`currencyDefaultRefusal` export — right**, one sentence for both renderers, the mail dialect's remedy naming `currency:@currency_code` and the in-app one not, which is what each dialect accepts.
5. **`@objectstack/plugin-email` `RenderOptions.currency`; `render()` refuses a no-argument hole without it — right, and coherent with #26937.** `parseMailHole` keeps `arg` as the literal text after the colon (`@currency_code`) and adds `codePath` beside it, so the new `parsed.arg === undefined` guard never fires on a marked-path hole; that hole still resolves its code from the send's data first and hands `formatValue` a literal argument, which wins over `opts.currency`. The guard sits before the amount is read, as the `@path` value refusal does, and `EmailService.resolveAndRenderTemplate` wraps it with the template name and locale through the existing `TEMPLATE_INVALID:` catch. One refusal family, three causes (grammar, `@path` value, no default), one prefix.
6. **`@objectstack/spec` contracts: `SendTemplateInput.currency`, `RenderTemplateInput.currency`, `AutomationContext.currency` — right**, optional inputs, documented, with the `TEMPLATE_INVALID` docs naming the new cause and that it clears once the default is set, which distinguishes it from the republish-only causes.
7. **`@objectstack/service-messaging`: `EmailChannelOptions.getTenantCurrency` / `InboxChannelOptions.getTenantCurrency`, wired through `resolveLocalizationContext` — right.** That resolver returns `currency: coerceCurrency(...)` with no built-in fallback (only `timezone` and `locale` have one), so "no tenant default" is a real state and `undefined` means it. The read is keyed by the delivery's `organizationId`, which the notify node stamps from the run's `tenantId` (`notify-node.ts:1077`); an organization-less delivery resolves at global scope the way a request without an organization does. The refusal is graded permanent by the existing `TEMPLATE_INVALID` regex in `classifyError`. The `sys_notification_template` arm of the same channel is untouched, correctly: `template-renderer.ts`'s interpolator has no formatter pipe.
8. **`@objectstack/service-automation`: `setTenantCurrencyResolver`, `FlowTenantCurrencyResolver`, `renderTextSlot(…, currency)`, seeding in `resolveRunContext` — right.** Every `renderTextSlot` caller on `main` (http url and headers, notify title / message / actionUrl, screen texts, and the `end` refusal message and screen translations through `renderFlowTextSlot`) now passes `context.currency`; none is left on the old signature. A subflow and a map child spread the parent context (`subflow-node.ts:103`, `map-node.ts:188`), so the seeded value is inherited; a suspended run persists `context_json` whole (`suspended-run-store.ts:992`), so it survives a pause. The resolver is wired inside the block that already holds `engineQl`, so the read goes over the same engine as the grants resolver. The refusal is a `FlowTextTemplateError`, the guard class a `fault` edge may not swallow — the right class, since a re-run with the same metadata and the same setting cannot succeed.
9. **`@object-ui/core` / `react` / `plugin-grid`: `ActionRunner.setTenantCurrency`, `fillTemplateHoles(…, currency)`, `bulkConfirmText(…, currency)`, `useActionRunnerTenantCurrency` — right.** `useLocalization()` returns `{}` outside a provider and `currency` undefined when unconfigured (no `USD` anywhere in `LocalizationContext.tsx`), so the UI cannot format in a guessed currency either. With none, `fillTemplateHoles` returns the source — the fallback it already had for every engine refusal on `main`.
10. **Semantic entry `18.template-currency-no-argument-tenant-default` (D3) — right.** No text to rewrite; the question is intent; the entry says so and names the three remedies.
11. **Census left as written — right.** On `main`, outside tests, the only lines asserting US dollars for the no-argument form are `template-engine.ts:71` and `:84`, both changed here; the spec describes, the notify / screen config descriptions and `flow-text-slot-template.ts` show the spelling `{{ amount | currency }}` and claim no currency. The four USD-pinning tests are re-pinned to a supplied default and to the refusal.
12. **Tests pin the narrowing red/green on every leg**: formula (refusal when unset, empty, lowercase, not a code; whole-sentence refusal; authoring unchanged), mail (all three faces, double and triple braces, nothing sent, `@path` needs no default), messaging (exact `sendTemplate` / `renderTemplate` input, no `currency` key without one, permanent grade), automation (resolver read once per run with the tenant id; a carried value wins; unwired / empty / throwing read all refuse and emit nothing), ui (confirm, success and bulk copy in the default; shown as written without one). Nothing in the diff pins `$` anywhere.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the PR body and in `.changeset/26939-currency-tenant-default.md`; `minor` on every package the diff moves (`formula`, `plugin-email`, `spec`, `service-messaging`, `service-automation`, `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/react`, `@object-ui/plugin-grid`); a BREAKING banner with Before / Now / remedy and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered template-currency-no-argument-tenant-default`), matched by the semantic entry file. **Matches the diff.** The accept set at render shrinks (a hole that rendered now refuses when no default reaches it) and nothing an author can write is widened; the additions are optional inputs and exports that carry the default, the same shape #26937's changeset declared `no (narrowing)` with "the additions are exports only". `narrowed` over `semantic` is the rule's own precedence: the meaning moved (semantic) and a value is refused (narrowed), several ⇒ narrowed. The "Supersedes, in the same release" paragraph is right and needed: `.changeset/26660-currency-code-path-formula.md`, `26660-currency-code-path-plugin-email.md`, `26660-mail-hole-grammar-formula.md` and `26660-mail-hole-grammar.md` on `main` each still say the no-argument form formats in US dollars, and `check-empty-changeset` forbids editing them. The `Skills-docs:` line names the three docs pages and the reason no `skills/**` file changes; read against `main`, no skill teaches the dollar default. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` — with no tenant default, should a flow `screen` text render without a symbol instead of failing the node? Answered: A, keep.** The ruling's target (6464324887) is "render or send refuses with `TEMPLATE_INVALID`" in every dialect; a screen text is a render by the flow's one renderer, and every flow text slot already answers a guard refusal the same way. Action copy is not a second currency rule: the engine refuses there too, and `fillTemplateHoles` answers that refusal the way it answers every refusal on `main` — the source, because a client dialog has no error channel to the author. The split is between two renderers' pre-existing refusal semantics, not inside one, and a per-slot partial render in the engine would be a new rendering mode the ruling did not ask for. What is owed on the display leg is not a symbol-less render but the prescription (④ S1). No follow-up card.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[0]` (26660 changesets say USD) — accepted**, handled by the supersedes paragraph (②).
- **`out_of_scope_findings[1]` (#27217 edits the same `render()`) — noted; this record judges this tree only.** The two hunks are adjacent, not overlapping, in `plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts`.
- **PR body "Mail with no default dead-letters … Setting the default and re-sending is the remedy" — accepted with ④ S2.** A dead row is not replayed; a new send after the setting is the remedy, as for every other `TEMPLATE_INVALID`. The grade is wrong only for a read fault (S2).
- **PR body "Pending 26660 changesets" — accepted** (②).
- **Human Minimum item 3 unchecked** (no local `pnpm lint`): `Lint · ESLint` is green on this head; the repo-gate lint families were cancelled (below). Not a flag against the diff.
- **Premise** ("the dev re-measures on `origin/main`"): verified independently (① 11).
- **Check-runs on this head.** Green: `Lint · ESLint`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `PR-body guards`. **Not answered on this head**: every `Type Check ·` job, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, the three `Lint · scoped ·` jobs, `Build Core`, `Build UI Deps`, `Build Docs`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` — all `cancelled` at 12:45–12:47Z when the push of `cf826880` superseded this head (the `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test UI` rows read `failure` with no output: the roll-up of those cancellations, not a red gate). This record does not stand in for them: the derived families are owed by the head that superseded this one, whose `CI` and `Lint & Type Check` runs were in progress at review time. The dev's own `dispatch-gates --commands` run on the merge tree (121 families, all exit 0) is the dev's account, not a gate verdict.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`: the no-argument `currency` hole stays declared everywhere it was (the describes keep the spelling, authoring accepts it) and stays delivered wherever a tenant default reaches the render — the ruling's own definition of what it means. Where no default exists, the refusal is the ruling's ("SEND refuses … nothing formats in USD"), it names the hole, the setting and both remedies, and it clears by a settings change rather than a republish. That is the spec's refusal made real, not a capability taken away at the consumer. Tried to break it on the three faces named for this review:

**Surfaces where the meaning moves from USD to the tenant default with no word to the author.** Every one — `sys_email_template` faces through `sendTemplate` / `renderTemplate` and the two messaging channels, the flow text slots (notify, http, screen, end), action and bulk-action copy — is named in the changeset's Before / Now and in the D3 entry, which is the notice the ruling provides; no authoring door can know a tenant's setting, so a save-time warning is not available and the ruling did not ask for one. An organization whose default differs from the currency its amounts are in now sees its default where it saw dollars: a wrong currency for those amounts, silently, exactly as a currency field already shows them — the ruling chose this trade (fields and dashboards follow the same rule), and the remedy `currency:CODE` is in the entry. Accepted by ruling, not by this record's preference. No surface outside the declared set moves: the messaging `sys_notification_template` interpolator has no formatters; `ExpressionEngine` consumers in objectql, lint, the MCP validate tool and the flow simulator compile or evaluate CEL, never render a template hole; the `tmpl` helper's envelopes land in the slots above.

**Can "refused at send" strand stored templates or flows with no prescription?** For the declared paths, no: the mail row dead-letters with a message naming the hole, `localization.currency`, `currency:EUR` and `currency:@currency_code`; the flow run fails with the same sentence through `FlowTextTemplateError`; the next send or run after the setting succeeds because both hosts read the default per delivery / per run (the automation read is once per run, at setup). Three edges strand, each short of a must-fix:

- **S1 — should-fix — `fillTemplateHoles` discards the refusal.** `ui/packages/core/src/actions/actionCopyTemplate.ts` returns the source when `filled.ok` is false and drops `filled.error`. On this leg the viewer sees `Reprice {{ amount | currency }}?` and nobody is told why: the only surface where the ruling's prescription does not reach anyone. Pre-existing shape for every refusal, so not a must-fix, but this PR is the first to route a refusal there by design. Log the refusal (`console.warn` or the runner's logger) with the sentence `currencyDefaultRefusal` builds, so the author has the remedy on the display leg too. This also closes the open question without a follow-up card.
- **S2 — should-fix — a transient read fault is graded permanent.** `getTenantCurrency` in `messaging-service-plugin.ts` returns `undefined` both when the organization has no default and when `resolveLocalizationContext`'s direct `sys_setting` read hits a backend fault (that resolver never throws; it memoizes the fault for `LOCALIZATION_FAILURE_CACHE_TTL_MS` and answers `currency: undefined`). Within that window every templated delivery of the organization with a no-argument hole dead-letters as `TEMPLATE_INVALID` — permanent, not retried, with a sentence saying the organization "has none set, or the caller did not supply it" while it may well have one set. The channel's own `classifyError` doc defines permanent as "re-trying the identical delivery can never succeed until someone edits the template", which this case is not. Narrow window (the recipient lookup on `sys_user` must succeed while `sys_setting` fails) and the same degradation the `locale` leg has today (silently en-US), so should-fix: expose `backendFailed` from `resolveLocalizationContext` (a core seam) or have the resolver throw on it, and grade that throw retryable in the channel.
- **S3 — should-fix — a run suspended before this change resumes with no default.** The resumed leg takes `segmentContext` from the persisted `run.context` and never re-enters `resolveRunContext`, so a run parked before deploy carries no `currency`, and its next notify / screen with a no-argument hole refuses although the organization has a default — a refusal whose remedy (set the default) is already done. Seed in the resume path when the persisted context carries none, the same "when absent" rule setup uses. Pre-upgrade runs only; runs started after deploy persist the value (verified in `suspended-run-store.ts`).

Two further should-fixes from the cited code:

- **S4 — should-fix — the mail callers outside the messaging channels pass no default.** `plugin-auth` calls `email.sendTemplate` at six sites (invitation, verification, existing-account notice, organization invite, and so on) without `currency`, so a tenant-customized auth template with a no-argument hole refuses whatever the setting, and the refusal's first remedy does not apply to it. The contract puts the duty on the caller and the claim scoped the mail path to the two channels; auth mail carries no amounts and the card's census found no shipped template with the hole, so a gap in reach, not in the rule. Thread the organization's default through those calls, or say in `SendTemplateInput.currency`'s doc which callers do.
- **S5 — should-fix — a misattributed warning on the translated leg.** `renderFlowTextSlot` catches the `FlowTextTemplateError` the translated template throws and logs "the translation … does not compile … Fix the translation's holes", then renders the authored text, which throws the same refusal. For a missing default both throws are the same sentence and the log line blames the translation. Skip the warning, or reword it, when the authored text throws the identical refusal.

Nothing found that formats in a guessed currency, nothing that refuses a hole which names its code, and the `@path` form of #26937 is untouched in behaviour and named in the refusal's remedy. No must-fix.

Head `9727b5111f709fcd92d512e40cc3cbf145662564`. Card #26939, claim `6465560284`, ruling `6464202770`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, narrowing face. Record `6469598248` at `645d56ff` is a PASS with no must-fix. The no-argument `currency` hole stays declared, and it is delivered wherever a tenant default reaches the render. The refusal without one is the ruling's own. The mail renderer is coherent with #26937's `currency:@path`. The open question was answered as A: keep the split between screen text (the node fails) and action copy (shown as written).
- **Should-fixes:**
  - S1 (`063f9608`): `fillTemplateHoles` now logs the refusal once per distinct sentence, naming the hole and the remedy.
  - S3 (`063f9608`): a resumed segment whose persisted context has no `currency` is seeded in `resolveDecisionSegmentContext`, on a copy. A cold-resume test goes red without it.
  - S5 (`063f9608`): `renderFlowTextSlot` renders the authored text before it blames a translation. When both refuse alike, the authored refusal answers and no translation warning is logged. Its test goes red on the old body.

A `sendTemplate` that names no `currency` gets the named organization's default, or the deployment-wide one for identity mail, through `resolveLocalizationContext`. A named currency is kept, and a failed or empty read adds nothing. `@objectstack/plugin-auth` joins the changeset.
  - S2 (a settings read fault graded permanent) needs a core seam. It is filed as #27257 and named in the body as the residual.
  - The changeset supersedes the four pending `26660-*.md` USD sentences in the same release.
